title: Convoy MOMA-01, 12 July 1944
eyebrow: East of Luzon · GUARDFISH's pack, Capt. W. V. O'Regan in GUARDFISH

paras.text: THRESHER found a southbound convoy on the night of 11 July and the four boats closed on it. APOGON attacked first, at 0304 on the 12th (Tokyo time), heard three hits and was rammed by a freighter of the convoy, bending her periscope shears; PIRANHA attacked at 0656 and sank a troop transport. GUARDFISH and THRESHER tracked it and were driven off by its escort. The boats' war patrol reports beside the escort division's record, on one GMT clock.

One ship sunk, Nichiran Maru, an Army transport of 6,503 tons: the escort division's chart marks her at 0745 on the 12th at N18-?9 E122-?0, the Navy's summary at 0935 (or 0735). No damage is recorded for APOGON's hour or for the ship that rammed her. PIRANHA's attack is paired as a hit, APOGON's as no loss.

sections.heading: APOGON's damage, as the Bureau of Ships summarised it

paras.text: The Bureau's postwar brief of the ramming: "While conducting night periscope attack on Japanese convoy, Apogon was rammed from starboard by an enemy AK which passed directly overhead. Depth at time of collision was about 70 feet to keel. Boat was heeled 15° to port. Top of shears, both periscopes and SD and SJ radar masts were bent about 45° to port." Water came into the conning tower at about 30 gallons a minute; "Several depth charges were dropped as Apogon went deep but did no damage. Boat was then caught at 430 foot depth"; the patrol was ended (War Damage Report 58, Appendix I, p. 280) [[cite:wdr58:I/p280]]. It places her at 19-51N 123-04E, about 47 nm north-north-east (031°) of the attack position on her own sheet (19-11N 122-38E); where the Bureau's position came from is not said, and the sheet's is the one drawn.
From Takao on the 9th for Manila, by the chart; its size and escorts are blank there. The name MOMA-01 heads the chart's line; reading it as Moji–Manila is ours. Its own record: [[convoy:moma-01]].

Positions are each boat's own reckoning. THRESHER is drawn because she found the convoy and tracked it; she did not fire at it. GUARDFISH, the group commander's boat, tracked it too and is left off the map (the page draws three boats); her track is on her own page.
APOGON kept zone I (−9), the same as the Japanese records; PIRANHA zone G (−7) and THRESHER zone H (−8).

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (APOGON 74801303, PIRANHA 74832061, GUARDFISH 74819308, THRESHER 74855459). The 1st Surface Escort Division's July 1944 war diary and the Navy's July summary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). JANAC (1947), a postwar list. Coastline: Natural Earth.

outcome.note: Fired 0304 I on the 12th (the sheet types 0301; the narrative's 0304 fits the hits heard at 0306-45) at 19-11N 122-38E, six Mk 23s at the center column of a southbound convoy (course 180, 13-14 kt; 8 or 9 AKs including a large passenger freighter, at least 6 escorts); three hits heard, believed in the far port column; then rammed by a large AK of the center column, which APOGON thought should have "a large hole in port quarter"; two ships claimed damaged. The convoy is MOMA-01 (inferred from place and course): the only line on the diary's Philippines-route chart at sea east of northern Luzon that morning, southbound from Takao (9th) to Manila (about the 15th), and the convoy PIRANHA attacked at 0656 I at 18-33N 122-53E, 40 nm south-south-east of APOGON's position, as a 13-kt convoy would run in 3 h 52 min. Its one recorded loss is Nichiran Maru (日蘭丸), sunk at 0745 I at 18-?9N 122-?0E (J02; 0935 in the summary, J01), 4 h 41 min after APOGON's firing and about 40 nm south, an hour after PIRANHA's attack; JANAC (secondary) credits PIRANHA with her (janac:6/p29). Neither record has a ship torpedoed or damaged near 0300, and neither names the ship that rammed APOGON; the diary's July loss list gives five ships slightly damaged by submarines without dates (GUARDFISH Patrol 8, J07: 聖川丸, 海17, 第一小倉丸, だかあ丸, 日永丸), none tied to this convoy. No loss for APOGON's attack in the Japanese record; whether her hits were on Nichiran Maru before PIRANHA's is not in it

outcome.note: Fired 0456 G = 0656 I on the 12th at 18-33N 122-53E, three Mk 18s at a large passenger freighter leading the center column of a southbound convoy; two hits claimed and a sinking. The diary's chart marks Nichiran Maru (日蘭丸) sunk at 0745 I on the 12th, 49 minutes later, at 18-?9N 122-?0E (the minutes partly lost; the degrees agree), on the line of a convoy from Takao to Manila (head モマ01); the summary (J01) has her torpedoed and sunk, timed 0935. She carried Army troops, as PIRANHA saw ("loaded with troops"). No other submarine is known to have attacked that convoy that morning; GUARDFISH and THRESHER were to the north (PIRANHA's p07). JANAC (secondary) credits PIRANHA with Nichiran Maru (6,504) on the 12th at 18-33N 122-53E, this sheet's position (janac:6/p29). GUARDFISH's report has her attack heard at 0848 I, about two hours after the firing

paras.text: MOMA-01 is a line on the 1st Surface Escort Division's July 1944 chart of the Philippines north route (別表第七), headed モマ01: it leaves Takao on the 9th and reaches Manila about the 15th. Its escort and ship-count cells are blank. ("モマ" reads as Moji–Manila by the division's naming, モ for 門司 and マ for マニラ (inferred); the chart shows only its Takao–Manila leg.) Its one mark is Nichiran Maru, an Army transport carrying troops, sunk at 0745 on the 12th at 18-?9N 122-?0E (the second figures of the minutes are lost in the binding); the Navy's summary times her loss at 0935, north-west of Luzon as written ("N西方"), though the boats' positions put the convoy east of northern Luzon.

APOGON attacked it at 0304 I on the 12th at 19-11N 122-38E (three hits heard, then rammed by one of the convoy), and PIRANHA at 0656 I at 18-33N 122-53E (Nichiran Maru, by JANAC, secondary). That this was the convoy both boats attacked is inferred: the chart has no other line at sea there that morning, and the convoy's course (180, 13-14 kt) and the two positions agree. GUARDFISH and THRESHER tracked it but did not fire.
**Not yet found**: the convoy's ships and escorts, its sailing from Moji, Nichiran Maru's own movement log, and any record of the ship that rammed APOGON or of damage from APOGON's three hits.

words.description: 8 or 9 ship convoy with at least 6 escorts including Fleet destroyers. Convoy composed of large passenger freighter and other fast modern AKs. Fired 6 torpedoes at center column consisting of one large passenger freighter and two overlapping AKs.
words.damaged: 1 unidentified AK - 4000 tons (UN) 1 large AK - 7500 tons (EU). This target damaged by ramming on port quarter.
words.determined_by: Heard 3 torpedo hits 2 Min. - 45 secs. after firing. Time indicates hits on far port column. Convoy scattered to starboard and was rammed by large AK of center column.
words.target_line: Target Draft 20 Course 180° Speed 13 Range 2000 (at firing)
words.type_attack: This was first attack on convoy which had been picked up by THRESHER. APOGON made end around and was in position as starboard flanker. GUARDFISH in contact on port side. Clear night, moonrise at 2345. Moon about 50% full. Due to visibility and escorts attack was made by periscope only. Submerged at 17,000 range. Was in position ahead of starboard column on 70° track for ships of center column. Binocular and TDC range checked at 2,000 yards. Fired six bow tubes small gyros spread by point of aim, three at large passenger freighter, fourth at overlapping ship ahead and beyond, fifth at overlapping ship astern and sixth back at MOT of first target. It is believed that all torpedoes missed center column and three hits were obtained on ships of far port column. No explosions seen. Misses were probably caused by a zig toward after firing. After torpedo explosions large AK of center column turned on red truck light and changed course to about 290 or 300° T. I thought he would pass well clear but he evidently sighted periscope wake and turned back to ram us. From our own damage believe he should have a large hole in port quarter. This attack probably would have been more successful if firing had been delayed another minute to get better track.
words.hits: Total of 3 hits heard commencing 2 min. 45 sec. after firing No. 1.
words.torpedo_detail: Mk. 23 torpedoes, Mk. 6-4 exploders, actuation Contact, Mk. 16-1 war heads, Torpex.
words.spread: Longitudinal on center target, MOT, bow and stern. One for right freighter, one for left freighter and last at MOT of center freighter.
words.note: The sheet types 0301 I; the narrative (p32) has 0255 "Swung right to a 70° track on center ships" and 0304 "Commenced firing 6 Mk. 23 torpedoes forward, estimated range 2,000 yards. Gyros between 355 and 010" (355 there, 356 on the sheet). Narrative 0306-45 "heard the first of three explosions 8 to 10 seconds apart", which it takes for hits in the far port column; the ramming followed (no time typed; the depth charges a few seconds after, seven in all). The sheet's 2 min. 45 sec. from firing matches 0304 + 2-45 = 0306-45, so the narrative's 0304 is the firing time and the sheet's 0301 is three minutes early. The sheet's position 19-11N 122-38E sits about 40 miles south of the 2314 contact (19-51N 123-04E), as a convoy making 13-14 kts on 180 for four hours would. Target data are the one solution typed for the center column (draft 20, course 180, speed 13, range 2000).

words.type_attack: Submerged periscope attack from ahead. Submerged 20,000 yards ahead of convoy at dawn. Convoy disposed in 3 columns zigging 40 degrees either side of base course of 180°(T). Made approach on leading ship of center column. Aircraft patrol made cautious use of periscope necessary. Depth control poor due to currents causing varying densities in water. At a range of about 3000 yards angle on bow was small turned out for stern tube shot. Didn't fire bow tubes because of poor depth control was unable to locate target in outboard column.
words.description: 1 - Large Passenger Freighter KMFKMK similar to ASAHASAN MARU (M.C.)
words.determined_by: Heavy explosion at 2'-00" and 2'-10" after firing. Target was loaded with troops no depth charges dropped in vicinity of target which substantiates opinion target was sunk and troops were in the water. Target was not sighted after coming back to periscope depth although convoy was still in sight. One ship remained in vicinity of attack for several hours and from its movements and escorts (2 DD's and one smaller escort) was probably rescuing survivors. Very loud breaking up noises and minor explosions heard for about 45 minutes thru hull and over sound gear. Large oil slick passed thru on following morning in vicinity of the attack.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 21' Course: 162 Speed: 11 Range: 2100 (At firing)
words.torpedo_detail: Mark 18-1 torpedoes, Mark 8-5 exploders, actuation set Mech. (actual Miss, Mech., Mech.), Mark 18-1 warheads, TPX.
words.note: Typed track 72 P; own course + gyro + 180 - target course gives about 80.5 P for tube 7 (read twice: kept as typed). The narrative (p08, 0401-0456) has the target as "a large AP and the only ship in sight not smoking", leading the center column, with #10 tube out of commission (bent spindle) so only three torpedoes were ready aft; "Heard two explosions". The narrative (p09) names the ship "similar to Asakasan Maru page 86, ONI 208-J"; the sheet types ASAHASAN MARU. The sheet's position is 18-33N 122-53E; ship contact 8 (p21, the convoy at 0250 G) is 18-55N 122-46E, course 170, 11 kt, remarks "Sank one AP".
